Last month, OpenAI previewed a hardware product under the Codex brand. Today, they officially unveiled the result of a collaboration with Work Louder: a Codex Micro keyboard priced at US$230.

Here's the product introduction:

The keyboard comes in two versions: a tactile (clicky) version and a silent version.

The website description reads: "Each Agent key displays different RGB lighting effects based on Codex's real-time status, so you can tell at a glance which is thinking, which is running, which is queued, and which has finished — then switch conversations accordingly."

The product page also lists three Codex-exclusive features:

  • On-demand skill triggering: Flip a toggle to launch frequently used Codex workflows, such as reviewing PRs (pull requests), debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Centralised core operations: Command keys provide dedicated shortcuts for your most-used actions, including accept, reject, press to talk, start new conversation, and more. Reduce window-switching and work more efficiently.
  • Adjust compute power on the fly: Twist the knob to instantly adjust the reasoning level. Keep it high for simple tasks, crank it up for jobs that need deeper thinking.
